title: Reservation Symphony: quarterly roadmap for dedicated pools & adaptive scaling
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Summary: 'Reservation Symphony' is a quarterly plan to unify how we reserve, warm, and gracefully spillover dedicated GPU pools while introducing an adaptive autoscaler that balances latency SLOs and unit cost. The initiative covers policy primitives, telemetry, canary mechanics, and a small pilot (two customers and internal sandbox) to validate economics and failure modes.

Objectives: 
- Provide predictable latency for P1 dedicated customers during burst scenarios (p50/p95 targets)
- Reduce unused reservation cost by 10-20% through adaptive warm-pools and reservoir scheduling
- Ship a safe canary+fallback rollout path so product teams can opt into adaptive autoscale with clear cost/regression guardrails

Scope (this quarter):
- Policy primitives: reservation tiers, prewarm windows, hedged fallback lanes, and per-customer surge corridors.
- Adaptive autoscaler MVP: signal collection, decision engine (simple policy rules + ML heuristic), and a single fallback path to shared-hosted tier.
- Observability: per-pool SLO dashboards, per-customer cost attribution, and an autoscale decision log surface in Console.
- Playbooks: operator runbooks for oncall, canary checklist, and customer enablement materials (FAQ + pricing examples).

Success metrics and acceptance criteria: 
- Latency SLO: p95 < 200ms for small gen models and < 800ms for long-seq transcode flows under canary customer workloads.
- Cost: 10% reduction in average idle-GPU-hours for pilot customers vs baseline week.
- Reliability: automated fallback triggers < 1 false-positive per 100k decisions in pilot.
- Ops readiness: runbook complete, oncall drill executed, canary rollback < 15 minutes.

Milestones (quarterly slices):
- Discovery (Weeks 1-3): finalize signal list, economic model, and pilot customer commitments. Deliverable: Confluence plan + cost model spreadsheet.
- Implementation (Weeks 4-8): infra hooks for reservoir scheduler, autoscale decision engine, SLO metrics pipeline. Deliverable: feature branch + infra PR.
- Pilot (Weeks 9-11): enable 2 pilot accounts, run synthetic surge scenarios and production shadowing. Deliverable: pilot report with performance/cost numbers.
- Canary & Rollout (Week 12): soft launch with 10% of eligible dedicated pools and runbook signoff. Deliverable: canary dashboard and launch postmortem template.

Key trade-offs identified: 
- Aggressiveness vs cost: tighter downscaling saves cost but increases warm-up risk (latency spikes). We will prioritize conservative downscales in early pilots.
- Complexity vs safety: MVP uses rule-based heuristics to avoid ML opaqueness; we defer heavier ML-driven prediction to follow-up cycles.
- Per-customer customization: full customization increases surface area; initial rollout offers 3 presets (conservative, balanced, aggressive) with ability to request custom policy.

Open questions and decisions needed: 
- What SLO budget should apply to shared-hosted fallback for customers on aggressive presets? (Decision by 2026-01-20)
- Minimum reservation window length for prewarm to be cost-effective on GPU families (data from Infra required).

Artifacts & links: 
- Confluence plan: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DCO/Reservation+Symphony+Q1+2026
- Cost model spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-reservoir-cost-model
- Implementation PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reservoir-scheduler/pulls (tracking list)
- Canary dashboards (temp): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/pilot/reservation-symphony

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Autoscale decision flapping during noisy signals. Mitigation: add hysteresis and minimum dwell time.
- Risk: Incorrect cost attribution confusing billing. Mitigation: parallel dry-run mode for 2 billing cycles before chargeable launch.
- Risk: Customer intolerance to latency spikes during rollout. Mitigation: fallback lane and explicit opt-in with clear SLA language.

Next steps (owner-level): 
- PM: finalize pilot customer list and required telemetry by 2026-01-16 (Riley Chen).
- Eng infra: surface per-GPU idle-hour metric and implement reservation API by 2026-01-30 (ENG owners).
- Eng runtime: expose warm-pool hooks and KV-cache priming endpoint by 2026-02-07.
- Ops: draft canary runbook and rollback playbook by 2026-02-14.

This ticket is the canonical quarterly plan for the initiative; individual engineering tasks will be tracked under ENG- and DES- issues with specific implementation details.
